name: Language-based Security
description:
Syllabus:
- run-time organization of programs
- code injection attacks and defenses
      - buffer overflows and stack canaries
      - control-flow hijacking and control-flow integrity
- code re-use attacks and defenses
      - return-oriented programming and software diversity
      - counterfeit object-oriented programming (COOP)
      - just-in-time return-oriented programming (JIT-ROP)
      - address-oblivious code reuse (AOCR)
- transient execution attacks:
      - Spectre-PHT, Spectre-BTB, Spectre-RSB
      - Spectre-defenses
- DRAM attacks, Rowhammer
      - Rowhammer attacks targeting software-state integrity (primarily Drammer)
- data attacks
      - non-control data attacks and data-flow integrity/randomization
- current topics
      - theoretical limits of control-flow integrity
      - trends in software diversity

Relevant aspects of the lecture will be complemented by lab assignments. The lab assignments focus on implementing defenses in a small compiler (QBE). Candidate defenses are:
- Buffer overflows and stack canaries
- Code reuse and software diversification:
  - instruction granularity (e.g., NOP insertion)
  - super-instruction granularity (e.g., basic block randomization)
  - timing-based side channels/Spectre attacks & defenses.

For more up to date information: https://langsec.ucsrl.de/
prerequisites:
IN2227 - Compiler Construction I
IN2040 - Virtual Machines
IN2209 - IT Security
